summary: This JUnit test class checks two behaviours of the Thermostat class: that a cold room in normal mode reports "Heating", and that in eco mode a slightly cool room of 66 degrees is left alone as "Idle" because eco mode tolerates cooler temperatures before it turns the heat on.

lines.text: Brings in the @Test annotation from JUnit 5, which is how you mark a method as a test the test runner should execute.
A static import lets you write assertEquals(...) directly instead of Assertions.assertEquals(...), keeping the tests short and readable.
Test code lives in its own class, separate from Thermostat itself, so the production class stays free of test scaffolding.
Test method names describe the expected behaviour in words, so a failure report tells you what broke without you having to read the body.
Sets up the scenario: a temperature of 60 with eco mode switched off.
Asserts that the status matches the expected value; the expected result comes first and the actual result second.
The new test added by the AI, covering the eco mode branch that the first test never touches.
Uses 66 degrees with eco mode on — a temperature that would trigger heating in normal mode but sits above the lower eco threshold.
Confirms eco mode holds off on heating at 66 degrees, which is exactly the difference the feature was meant to introduce.
